Row bk_mose1_as_025 of the settlers table prints the year 1823 against his name, agreeing with the hiring this field already records; it corroborates and does not promote.

origin.note: A DRAWN REGION IS REPLACED BY A PRINTED NATIVITY. This field held 'New England', drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a survivorship sample carrying `replaceable_by` 'a source that says where this household came from'. This is that source. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1895), printed pages 78-79, the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830 (data/research/books/records/moses_kirkland_v1_actual_settlers_pre_1830.json). It is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8 three lines above itself, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified, so NOTHING READ OFF IT IS GRADED ABOVE `inferred` HERE. Row bk_mose1_as_025 reads 'McKee, David', nativity Va, YEAR 1823, remarks 'Paid taxes in 1825, voted in 1826'. THE YEAR IS THE CHECK ON THE NATIVITY: 1823 is the year this card already carries for his hiring under the treaty obligation, so the row is right about the one column the layer can test it on. INFERRED AND NOT ATTESTED: 1895, at second hand, transcription_mediated, and the crosswalk's own merge rests on both records putting a David McKee at Chicago in the 1820s in a settlement this table sizes at thirty-six households. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: the table's own preamble bounds it BEFORE 1830 and its remarks are civic acts of 1825-1830. A man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01, and this edit moves no residence, no `present_on_scene_date` and no grade. The identity is the books crosswalk's landed merge (T-0961) and is not re-opened here.

last_dated_appearance.note: NO SIGHTING, SO THE LEG IS A SOURCE'S SPAN. The card holds no dated reading of this person at or before the scene date; the date here is the far end of what a cited source COVERS, which the role's own note calls the source's bound and not the man's. Read from `roles[] (source_span)` as `1673/1857`, which reaches 1857-12-31 — a window that covers 1835-07-01 itself, so it pins no last sighting before the day and cannot be read as one. THE FIELD IS THE EVIDENCE UNDER THE VERDICT, not a new claim: nothing here moves the presence off `uncertain`, and T-1159 and T-1172 classify this household by this date instead of reading it out of the prose (T-1144 acceptance 9).

present_on_scene_date.note: THE AGENCY ITSELF IS THE PROBLEM. Andreas's list of the establishment is written for the period of Owen's agency generally and not for 1835, and the treaty obligation that created the post was superseded by the cession of 1833. Whether a government smith for the Potawatomi was still at his anvil on 1 July 1835, six weeks before the removal, is not stated anywhere reached, and the value says so.

persons.name: David McKee

occupation.note: Government blacksmith to the Indian agency at Chicago. Andreas names the agency establishment under Col. Owen: sub-agents Kercheval and Stuart, 'Billy Caldwell (Sauganash) as interpreter; David McKee as blacksmith, and Joseph Porthier as striker'. The 1821 treaty obliged the United States to keep a blacksmith at Chicago for the Potawatomi and McKee was hired for that.

persons.note: HE IS THE NAMED OCCUPANT THIS DATASET'S GOVERNMENT SMITHY HAS BEEN MISSING. data/structures/blacksmith_shop_state_st.json describes 'a building known only as a clause in other people's sentences' with an empty occupants field; McKee is the man in the clause. Andreas's list of the settlement's residents puts 'small log buildings occupied by the blacksmith, Mr. McKee, and Billy Caldwell' in the vicinity of Cobweb Castle, and he signed the 1832 militia agreement. OLD SETTLERS, 1882 — A DATE OF DEATH, AND NOTHING ABOUT 1835. John Wentworth's roll of old settlers who had died since 1 January 1881, kept for the Calumet Club and printed in the Chicago Tribune of 25 April 1882, carries “David McKee, April 9, 1881.”. That corroborates a Chicago residence before 1840 and fixes the END of this life, which this record did not carry; it is not an arrival and it places nobody in the town on 1 July 1835. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json). THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “MCKEE DAVID”, 1830-09-27: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 1 of block 5 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L1BL5CHIOT, as printed); lot 7 of block 4 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L7BL4CHIOT, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $61.00 (ls1359, ls1360). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $61.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: MCKEE DAVID matches David McKee: the forename names David McKee of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as 'April 9, 1881' and the age as 'aged 80¼'. An age of 80 years and 3 months means at least that and less than 80 years and 4 months, so the birth falls between 1800-12-10 and 1801-01-09: the birth year is 1800 or 1801. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "McKee, David, died near Aurora, Ill., April 9, 1881, aged 80¼", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

research_note: THE MAN THE 1821 TREATY PAID TO SHOE POTAWATOMI HORSES, AT AN ANVIL THIS PROJECT MODELS. This household exists to close a loop the structures layer left open, and the presence field is where the honesty is: the shop is in the scene and the smith may not have been. STANDING CONSTRAINT. AGENTS.md: the final removal of the Potawatomi from Chicago occurred in August 1835, inside this project's first target year and six weeks AFTER the scene date; Native presence, representation and depiction are not research gaps to be filled by inference, and v1 ships no human figures at all. This record is a dataset entry that states what named sources say about a named person and adds nothing. It carries review_required so that no scene containing it can be marked released before the consultation the project has committed to.

old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
